newsitem.title: UK: French stocks hit record, Nikkei falls.
newsitem.headline: French stocks hit record, Nikkei falls.

text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended Thursday.

LONDON - Shares ended lower as recent volatility on Wall Street prompted a small pull-back from Wednesday's record highs. Fears that the Dow could be on the verge of a substantial downward correction weighed on investor sentiment but steady British and U.S. interest rates helped calm but not eradicate jittery market nerves. The FTSE 100 index of leading shares closed 15.6 points down at 4,265.9.

FRANKFURT - Germany's DAX index of 30 leading shares posted modest gains as selective interest in the chemical sector continued and the Bundesbank's decision to leave rates unchanged matched expectations. The 30-share DAX rose 6.14 points to end the bourse session at 3,104.14 points. In post-bourse trade the index rose 10.05 to 3,124.78.

PARIS - French stocks reversed their early losses and rallied to a second consecutive record close after the bourse shrugged off weakness on Wall Street and took its lead from rising European stock markets. The blue-chip CAC-40 index rose 17.18 points to a closing record of 2,558.43 points.
ZURICH - Shares edged to another closing high as profit taking in Roche was offset by buying in bank shares. The broad SPI advanced 3.36 points to 2,742.39.

TOKYO - The stock market's key barometer closed lower but kept its nose above the psychologically important 18,000 level. Brokers said the market had not recovered completely from a tumble in the banking sector on Wednesday, although global blue-chips were sought. The Nikkei 225 average ended 147.54 points lower at 18,038.43.

HONG KONG - The stock market was closed today for the beginning of the Chinese lunar new year holiday. On Wednesday, the Hang Seng index closed 112.07 points higher at 13,660.50. The market will reopen on February 10.

SYDNEY - A mixed share market closed barely changed. The All Ordinaries index lost 0.6 points to 2,435.2. Brokers said the finish was better than expected with the market holding the line in the face of a weak Wall Street, a bond market battered by stronger than expected wages data and a disappointing News Corp. first half net profit.

JOHANNESBURG - Shares surged in an all-time high volume of trade. The market swiftly ignored early jitters over an overnight fall on Wall Street and rapidly gained ground that it held until the end of trade when it finished at its day highs. The all-share index ended up 59.5 points at 6,863.6 as the industrial index rose 47.0 points to 8,180.4. The gold index added 13.7 points to 1,387.4.
